To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that
the GxxxGxGGxxxG motif of type-1 vertebrate VDAC is a dimerization motif, that it is also involved in channel gating, and that it is a cholesterol binding site.

(a) the N-terminal voltage-sensor of human VDAC is a cholesterol-binding domain, (b) the N-terminal sensor is a cholesterol-binding site of type-1 porin, and (c) the N-terminal VDAC sensor is a cholesterol binding domain of type-1 channel.

the GxxxGx motifs at the N-terminal voltage-sensor of cell membrane-standing human VDAC and on the β-sheets 9 and 19 of mitochondrial outer membrane-anchored VDAC are relevant for the function of the porin channels and, furthermore, that the Gxxx motifs are relevant for amyloid Aβ peptide induced apoptosis.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the function of the GxxxG and the GxxxGx motifs of type-2 VDAC.
the relevance of GxxxG stretches in the molecular structure of VDAC/eukarian porin.
the molecular biology of VDAC and the relevance of GxxxG and GxxxGx motifs in this channel.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that

the glycine motifs found in the N-terminal voltage-sensor and in the β-barrel of type-1 porin channel are of utmost importance for channel gating, channel dimerization/agregation, cholesterol binding, and channel function.

the GxxxGx motif on the proximal N-terminal voltage sensor, the GxxxGG motif at β-sheet 19 and the GxxGxxxGG motif on β-sheet 9 of type-1 human VDAC, all together, are relevant in channel function, apoptosis induction and Alzheimer's disease.
the GxxxG and GxxxGx motifs on type-1 VDA C's N-terminus, as well as on β-sheet 9, and β-sheet 19 are of relevance to the function of the channel and, thus, the channel protein.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
the GxxxGx motif of the N-terminal stretch of human type- 1 VDAC is not a nucleotide binding motif, but a cholesterol binding motif.
the N-terminal voltage-sensor of human type-2 VDAC is a dimerization motif, which, in the case of human type- 1 VDAC, might be engaged in apoptosis-induction via amyloid Aβ.
the N-terminal voltage sensing part of type-1 human VDAC is a highly relevant target for amyloid Aβ peptide binding, and thus for apoptosis induction, in the course of Alzheimer's disease.
The main takeaway from our work is that
the GxxxG sequence motif on β-sheet 9 is the more relevant of both.
the GxxxGx motif on β-sheet 9 and the GxxxG and GxxGCxxxG motifs on β-sheets 19 and 9, respectively, may also contribute to the function of the channel.
the N-terminal voltage-sensor of type-1 porins is an aggregation site of amyloid Aβ and that the channel's β-sheets 9 and 19 may also be involved in the process.
